title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 12
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 12: remembering your Creator in youth, the silver cord and golden bowl, and the end of the matter - fear God and keep his commandments.

questions.text: Whom should you remember in the days of your youth?
questions.explanation: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come.

questions.text: What happens to the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars in the days this chapter describes?
questions.explanation: The chapter speaks of the time before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain.

questions.text: Why do the mourners go about the streets, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says that man goes to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets.

answers.text: Because man goes to his everlasting home
Because the city has been destroyed

questions.text: In the picture of verse 6, what is broken at the cistern?
questions.explanation: The verse speaks of the time before the silver cord is severed, the golden bowl is broken, the pitcher is broken at the spring, or the wheel broken at the cistern.

questions.text: When the dust returns to the earth as it was, where does the spirit return?
questions.explanation: The dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

answers.text: To the dust of the earth
To the clouds after the rain

questions.text: What does the Preacher say in this chapter about all things?
questions.explanation: "Vanity of vanities," says the Preacher. "All is vanity!"

questions.text: Because the Preacher was wise, what did he do for the people?
questions.explanation: Because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge, and he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.

answers.text: He taught them knowledge and set in order many proverbs
He judged all their disputes at the gate of the city
He built houses and planted vineyards for the people
He led the people out of the city into the wilderness

questions.text: What are the words of the wise compared to in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The words of the wise are like goads, and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies.

questions.text: What does this chapter say about making many books?
questions.explanation: Of making many books there is no end, and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

answers.text: It is the duty of the wise
There is no end to it
It should be left to the scribes

questions.text: According to the end of the matter, what is the whole duty of man?
questions.explanation: The end of the matter is this: fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man.

answers.text: To eat, drink, and be joyful
To seek wisdom under the sun
To fear God and keep his commandments
